name: Taqueria La Morena
why: A family taqueria serving downtown South San Francisco since 1986, known locally for big carne asada super burritos. Few written sources beyond its own site.
story: A family-owned taqueria on Baden Avenue in the old downtown of the Industrial City, open since 1986 and doing catering for the businesses east of the freeway. The menu is the classic taqueria run of tacos, quesadillas suizas and super burritos, and opens early on weekends.
hours: Mon to Fri 9:30 am to 8:30 pm; Sat and Sun 8 am to 8:30 pm (own site)
flags: Carne asada super burrito as the favorite comes from listing-site summaries.
Consider dropping unless a visit finds more to say.

name: Deli Board
why: A takeout-only SoMa counter that stacks two or three meats per roll, with paper-thin pastrami as the anchor. Pricey at $18-23 a sandwich.
story: Adam Mesnick started Deli Board in 2009 and moved it to this Folsom Street counter two years later. The rule is more is more: corned beef, pastrami and salami on one roll, or bacon over tuna salad, dressed in house Board or Mick sauce, with a fat pickle on the side. Daily specials go further over the top.
order: The Allison, or anything built on the Romanian pastrami.
flags: Founding (2009) and move to 1058 Folsom (2011) come from a search summary; Hoodline 2015 profile not fetched.
Owner runs a polarizing SoMa street-conditions social account (Chronicle, 2023); possible brand fit issue for Dan.
Price point is high for this list.
Confirm still open in 2026: newest fetched source is Feb 2024.
